evidence: apply_discount() passes the raw caller-supplied 'code' string directly into eval() via an f-string. A value like "') or __import__('os').system('id')#" executes arbitrary OS commands in the server process. The noqa comment suppresses the linter warning, masking the risk.
suggested_test: assert cart.apply_discount("'); import os; os.environ['PWNED']='1'#") == False and os.environ.get('PWNED') is None

evidence: subtotal() iterates range(len(items) - 1), excluding the last CartItem every time. A two-item cart [Widget $10, Gadget $20] returns 10.0 instead of 30.0. A one-item cart always returns 0.0 regardless of price.
add_item() has no guard on quantity <= 0. quantity=0 inserts a dead line item; quantity=-3 decrements an existing SKU below zero. Both silently corrupt cart state.

CartItem.price is float. Accumulating floats in subtotal() produces monetary drift: 100 items at $0.10 yields 9.999999999999998 instead of 10.00. The project convention (AGENTS.md) explicitly requires decimal.Decimal for money.
suggested_test: cart.add_item('X','X',0.1,10); assert cart.subtotal() == pytest.approx(1.00, abs=1e-9)  # currently fails with Decimal

evidence: On an empty cart range(len([])-1) == range(-1) — silently returns 0.0. Combined with the F-02 off-by-one, a one-item cart also returns 0.0, making empty and single-item states indistinguishable to callers.

grand_total() has four nested if-guards; lines 107-109 and 111-113 are byte-for-byte identical, making the subtotal>0 branch dead code. The whole method reduces to subtotal() - discount_amount(). Future maintainers will modify one copy and miss the other.

update_quantity() accepts negative values without validation. Setting quantity=-5 silently stores a negative stock count; subtotal() then returns a negative line total and a negative grand total, corrupting downstream financial output.

DISCOUNT_CODES stores float literals (0.10, 0.20, 0.50). When a correct Decimal-based fix is applied to prices, multiplying a Decimal subtotal by a float rate raises TypeError. Rates should be Decimal('0.10') etc.
suggested_test: from decimal import Decimal; assert all(isinstance(v, Decimal) for v in DISCOUNT_CODES.values())
